cards.explanation: The answer is being alive. Jesus tells Sardis, “you have a reputation for being alive, yet you are dead.” A reputation is what a church is known for, and for Sardis that was being alive. I've seen cookies that looked golden and finished on the cooling rack and turned out raw in the middle, so I know how looks can fool you, friends. Jesus sees past the outside.

The word is dead. Jesus says, “you have a reputation for being alive, yet you are dead.” That's a hard sentence to hear, friends. I think it's also why the next thing He says is “Wake up.” He's speaking straight to them, and He isn't done with them yet.

The first thing Jesus tells Sardis to do is wake up. He says, “Wake up and strengthen what remains, which is about to die…” Wake up comes first, and after that comes the work of strengthening what's left. A church called dead gets an alarm clock before it gets anything else.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “…I have found your deeds incomplete in the sight of My God.” He doesn't say complete. The first part is true: He tells them to strengthen what remains, which is about to die. So this one is half true and half not.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “If you do not wake up, I will come like a thief, and you will not know the hour when I will come upon you.” So they will not know the hour. That's why waking up matters. This is also why I keep my ovens ready, friends, because no one knows the day (Matthew 24:36).

The answer is like a thief. Jesus says, “If you do not wake up, I will come like a thief…” He adds that they “…will not know the hour…” when He comes (Revelation 3:3). That's the point of the picture. It's a warning, and it comes with a way to be ready: wake up.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “But you do have a few people in Sardis who have not soiled their garments, and because they are worthy, they will walk with Me in white.” Even in a church called dead, He sees these few. He hasn't missed a single one of them. Walking with Him is the promise.
The answer is True. Jesus says, “And I will never blot out his name from the Book of Life…” That's a promise to the one who overcomes. Never means never, friends. I'd hold onto that one tight.

The answer is His Father and His angels. Jesus says, “…I will confess his name before My Father and His angels.” He says the overcomer's name out loud in front of them. That's a name worth being known by.

The answer is that no one can shut them. Jesus says, “What He opens no one can shut, and what He shuts no one can open.” Nobody can overrule that key. Once He opens a door, it stays open. I spent years stuck in a junk drawer somebody else closed, so that line stands out to me.

The answer is an open door. Jesus says, “Behold, I have placed before you an open door, which no one can shut.” It matches what He said about the key. He opens it, and no one can shut it. It's placed right in front of them.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “I know that you have only a little strength, yet you have kept My word and have not denied My name.” So it's a little strength, not great strength. The yet in that sentence matters, because they still kept His word. Small can still be faithful.
The word is denied. Jesus says, “…you have kept My word and have not denied My name.” They had only a little strength and still didn't deny Him. That's a church I'd want in my bakery line.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “…I will make them come and bow down at your feet, and they will know that I love you.” The liars bow at the feet of the church in Philadelphia. The church isn't made to bow to them. And the point is that they will know He loves the church.

The word is loves. Jesus says, “…and they will know that I love you.” That's the end of the sentence, and it's the heart of it. To a church with only a little strength, He says He loves them. I can't think of a better word to end on, friends.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “Because you have kept My command to persevere, I will also keep you from the hour of testing that is about to come upon the whole world…” The because is right there in the verse. They kept His command, and He will keep them. That's a promise from Him.

The answer is so no one will take their crown. Jesus says, “I am coming soon. Hold fast to what you have, so that no one will take your crown.” The crown is the reason He gives. They're to hold on to what they have. That's the whole reason, plain as day.

The answer is the new Jerusalem. Jesus says, “…and the name of the city of My God (the new Jerusalem that comes down out of heaven from My God)…” The text names the city for us. It comes down out of heaven from His God. And the overcomer gets that name written on him.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “Upon him I will write the name of My God, and the name of the city of My God… and My new name.” So there are three names in all. His own new name is the last one. It's written on the one who overcomes.
